_readme: Japan overrides. Only keys that differ from data.base.json belong here. See DATA-CONTRACT.md. Japan uses TWO application documents: 'rirekisho' (a standardised personal-history form, photo and date of birth expected) and 'shokumu keirekisho' (a detailed reverse-chronological career-history document). The shell links one PDF, so cv.href points at the shokumu keirekisho — the rirekisho is sent with it, not instead of it. Both HTML sources live in '01 CV & Resumes/Sources (HTML & LaTeX)/Country/jp/'.
_todo: TODO(jp): no Japanese-language ability is stated anywhere on this page or in either document, because none has been supplied. Add a JLPT level (or 'no Japanese yet, studying') only after Prajwall confirms it. Japanese ability is screened on for almost every role in Japan, including English-speaking ones.

TODO(jp): set cv.href to assets/cv/jp-shokumu-keirekisho.pdf once the PDF is exported from Country/jp/shokumu_keirekisho_jp.html. Until the file is on disk the build omits the CV button from /jp/ rather than shipping a 404.

TODO(jp): the rirekisho needs a photo, a date of birth and a full postal address. None of the three are on this page (the site does not need them) but the printed rirekisho does. See Country/jp/NOTES-jp.md.

TODO(jp): meta.lang stays 'en' because strings.* are still English. Japanese section headings exist in the two printed documents, where the markup can carry lang='ja' on the Japanese runs. Do not put Japanese into strings.* here until (a) a native speaker has reviewed it and (b) meta.lang flips to 'ja' in the same commit — mixed-script text under lang='en' is read out wrongly by screen readers.
TODO(jp): confirm the portfolio/site origin used on the printed documents (site.origin says sprajwallnarayana.com; the older UK resume prints sprajwallnarayana.vercel.app). One of the two is stale.
TODO(jp): decide a salary expectation before applying. Japanese applications ask for it in the rirekisho's preferences box; it is currently left as an explicit placeholder.
headline: AI Engineer — product development and platform operations
summary: AI Engineer on the founding team at Colligence Research in Bengaluru. The work covers both halves of the system: the product — agentic and LLM pipelines, a code-generation service and the backend APIs behind them — and the platform it runs on, where I established the DevOps/SRE function and now lead it: CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, observability, incident response and authentication. I continue to ship product features alongside that. I am looking for an engineering role in Japan and would need **visa sponsorship**; the two Japanese application documents, rirekisho and shokumu keirekisho, are available on request.
workAuthorisation: Currently based in Bengaluru, India, with no existing right to work in Japan. The applicable status of residence is **Engineer / Specialist in Humanities / International Services**, the standard category for software engineers hired from overseas; a B.E. in Computer Science is a qualifying degree for it, and the Certificate of Eligibility is filed by the sponsoring employer.
typedPhrases: evaluation harnesses as CI merge gates
